entry.title: The SAP Fiscal Calendar, End to End: How It Gets Populated, How Data Loads in BW, and Where the ABAP
entry.content:
Every FI posting, every CO report and every BW query leans on the fiscal period — yet very few of us ever stop to trace where that period actually comes from and how it travels through the landscape. There is no "fiscal calendar load" job anywhere. So how does the fiscal calendar get populated, how does it function through every data load, and where does ABAP actually run in all of this? The short answer: it is born as configuration in ECC, derived onto every document at posting time, physically copied into BW as global settings, stamped onto every record BW extracts — and for the time characteristics themselves, served virtually by ABAP classes with no master data load at all. Let's walk through each stage.

Stage 1 — It starts as configuration, not data (OB29)

Fiscal calendars in ECC are controlled by the Fiscal Year Variant, configured via transaction OB29 and used across FI, CO and MM. Nobody uploads fiscal calendar data — the moment a variant is defined and its periods maintained in OB29, the system populates a small family of Customizing tables behind the scenes:

Table

Purpose

T009

Fiscal year variant (header) — variant ID, number of posting periods, year-dependent flag, calendar year flag

T009B

Period dates per fiscal year variant — start/end date for each posting period (and special periods)

T009C

Assignment of company code shortened fiscal year (used when a fiscal year is shortened, e.g., mid-year go-live)

T009T

Fiscal year variant texts (descriptions)

T009Y

Fiscal year variant — year-dependent version (if the calendar-year-dependent flag is set, periods can differ by year)

 

Two variants you will meet on almost every project: K4 (calendar year — 12 posting periods plus 4 special periods, where period 001 = January) and V3 (April to March — the standard variant for India and several other countries, where period 001 = April). K4 barely needs T009B at all because periods equal calendar months; V3 is where the real mechanics of the table come into play.

The year shift — the small entry that makes non-calendar fiscal years work

For a variant like V3, each month entry in T009B carries not only a period number but also a year shift (annual displacement) of -1, 0 or +1. This is the entry that tells the system which fiscal year a calendar month belongs to. Under V3, April through December carry shift 0 — a posting on 15.05.2026 lands in period 002 of fiscal year 2026. But January through March carry shift -1 — a posting on 15.01.2027 lands in period 010 of fiscal year 2026, because it still belongs to the fiscal year that started in April 2026. This one column is the entire secret behind non-calendar fiscal years, and it is exactly what downstream systems consume rather than recalculate.

One neighbouring concept worth separating out: the fiscal calendar is not the factory calendar (table TFACS, maintained via SCAL). The factory calendar defines working days and holidays for logistics and scheduling; the fiscal calendar defines posting periods for accounting. Both travel to BW as global settings, but they answer completely different questions.

Stage 2 — How the calendar reaches documents (assignment and derivation)

Configuration alone doesn't put a fiscal period on anything. The variant first has to be assigned, and then the period is derived at posting time.

Table / Field

Context

T001-PERIV

Company code's assigned fiscal year variant

CSKS / CEPC etc.

Controlling objects inherit the fiscal year variant from the company code

BKPF-MONAT / GJAHR

Posting period and fiscal year on FI documents, derived using T009B logic

 

The derivation itself is simple: given a posting date plus the fiscal year variant, the system looks up T009B (applying the year shift) to determine which period the date falls into — periods 1 to 12, plus special periods 13 to 16 for adjustments and audit. This is done via standard function modules such as FIRST_DAY_IN_PERIOD_GET, LAST_DAY_IN_PERIOD_GET and DATE_TO_PERIOD_CONVERT. The result (MONAT, GJAHR) is stamped onto the document. Special periods are never derived from a date — periods 13 to 16 are entered manually by the user during year-end closing, which is why a posting date in March can sit in period 013.

In other words, the fiscal period on a document is not stored calendar data — it is computed once at posting time from the T009B rules and then persisted on the document itself. This detail is exactly what makes the BW side behave the way it does.

Stage 3 — How the fiscal calendar physically reaches BW: Transfer Global Settings

Here is the part most people miss. BW does not query ECC's T009 tables remotely — it holds its own local copy of them. When a source system is connected, the administrator runs Transfer Global Settings (in RSA1, right-click the source system). This function copies the source system's global Customizing — fiscal year variants (T009/T009B), currencies (TCUR*), units of measure (T006*) and factory calendars — into identically structured tables inside the BW system itself.

So the fiscal calendar is populated in BW not through a DataSource or an InfoProvider, but as replicated Customizing sitting quietly in BW's own T009/T009B. BW never uses these tables as reporting data — it uses them as the rulebook for time conversion and for query runtime logic, which we'll see below. This is also why the transfer has to be repeated whenever the variant configuration changes in the source: BW's copy does not update itself.

Stage 4 — How the data load actually works in BW

With the rulebook in place, let's follow a transaction record end to end and see where fiscal time gets attached.

Step 1: Extraction — the data arrives already stamped

Business Content extractors in FI/CO (for example the General Ledger line-item extractors) read the documents where MONAT and GJAHR were already stamped at posting time. So the DataSource delivers fields like FISCVARNT and FISCPER pre-populated by ECC — the extractor is simply forwarding the result of the T009B derivation that happened when the document was posted. Nothing fiscal is computed during extraction.

Step 2: Staging and transformation — the classic load path

The record then follows the standard BW flow: DataSource → InfoPackage into the PSA → Transformation → DTP → target (DSO/ADSO or InfoCube). The transformation is where the source fields are mapped to the Time InfoObjects — FISCVARNT to 0FISCVARNT, FISCPER to 0FISCPER, the posting date to 0CALDAY, and so on.

Step 3: Automatic time conversion — where BW's local T009B earns its keep

Time characteristics enjoy a special privilege in BW transformations: automatic time conversion and derivation. If the source supplies only a date (0CALDAY) plus the fiscal year variant, BW can derive 0FISCPER, 0FISCPER3 and 0FISCYEAR automatically — and it performs that derivation using its local copy of T009B, transferred in Stage 3. The same mechanism derives 0CALMONTH, 0CALQUARTER and 0CALYEAR from 0CALDAY. This is precisely why a stale Transfer Global Settings shows up as wrong fiscal periods in BW: the derivation is only as correct as the local rulebook.

Step 4: Storage — where fiscal time finally lives in BW

Once loaded, the values settle into BW's own structures. In InfoCubes, each cube's time dimension table stores 0FISCPER, 0CALDAY and friends as dimension values, linked through SID tables; in DSOs/ADSOs they are simply fields on the record. If fiscal period hierarchies are built, they are stored like any hierarchy (e.g., /BI0/HFISCPER). From this point on, fiscal period is just another characteristic value — with one defined mapping into calendar dates, used mainly for display, sorting and hierarchy purposes.

InfoObject

Purpose

0FISCVARNT

Fiscal year variant (carried over from ECC's T009)

0FISCPER

Fiscal year/period combined (e.g., "2026001")

0FISCPER3

Fiscal period alone (3-char, e.g., "001")

0FISCYEAR

Fiscal year alone

0CALDAY

Calendar day

0CALMONTH

Calendar month (YYYYMM)

0CALWEEK

Calendar week

0CALQUARTER

Calendar quarter

0CALYEAR

Calendar year

 

Two modelling details worth knowing here. First, 0FISCPER is compounded to 0FISCVARNT — a period value like "001" is meaningless on its own, because period 001 is January under K4 but April under V3. The compounding forces every fiscal period value to carry its variant, which is why 0FISCVARNT must always be present (mapped or set as a constant) whenever 0FISCPER is filled in a transformation. Second, 0FISCPER is stored internally in the format YYYYPPP (e.g., 2026001) but displayed in external format (e.g., 001.2026) — a detail that regularly surprises people writing routines or filters against the raw value.

Where does ABAP actually run during a BW load?

A common mental model is "BW has classes, and data loads from those ABAP classes." The reality is more precise, and worth getting right: the load is driven by BW objects — DataSources, InfoPackages, Transformations, DTPs — and ABAP classes are the machinery that BW generates or ships to execute some of them. The classes are the engine room, not the source of the data.

On the extraction side, the code is mostly function modules, not classes: Business Content extractors run extraction function modules through the Service API (SAPI), and generic extractors built in RSO2 are based on a table/view, an InfoSet or a function module.

On the transformation side, classes genuinely appear — but they are generated by the system. When a transformation is activated, BW generates an ABAP program containing a local class, and every routine you write — start routine, end routine, field routine, expert routine — becomes a method of that generated class, working on parameters like SOURCE_PACKAGE and RESULT_PACKAGE. You write the method body; BW generates and owns the class around it. The DTP then executes this generated program at load time. Underneath all of it, the DTP framework, request handling and ADSO activation are implemented in SAP standard classes (the CL_RS* family) — framework code you never touch.

And a note for newer stacks: in BW/4HANA, a transformation without ABAP routines can be HANA-optimized — pushed down and executed entirely inside HANA as a calculation scenario, with no ABAP class running during the load at all. This is exactly why avoiding ABAP routines is a standard performance recommendation in that generation.

Why time characteristics have no master data load — virtual master data read classes

Open 0FISCYEAR in InfoObject maintenance and look at the Master data/texts tab, and you'll find the most elegant piece of this whole story. The setting Master Data Access is not "Default" — it is "Own Implementation", pointing to a master data read class: CL_RSMD_RS_0FISCYEAR.

"Default" would mean the InfoObject has physical master data tables (/BI0/P*, /BI0/T*) filled by data loads. "Own Implementation" means the opposite: the InfoObject has no stored master data at all. Whenever anyone needs its values — a query run, an F4 value help, a text display — the system calls this class at runtime and the values are generated on the fly. There is no DTP, no PSA, and no master data table filling up with a row for every year that has ever existed.

Why did SAP design it this way? Because fiscal years and periods are rule-based, not data-based. The set of valid fiscal years is trivially derivable, and fiscal periods are fully determined by the T009/T009B rules that BW already holds locally via Transfer Global Settings. Loading them as master data would mean materializing an infinite, rule-generated list. So SAP ships the time characteristics — 0FISCYEAR, 0FISCPER, 0CALDAY, 0CALMONTH and friends, each with its own CL_RSMD_RS_* class — with virtual master data access instead. The calendar was never data to begin with, and here that principle is implemented literally in code.

The distinction to keep sharp: transaction data still loads exactly as described in Stage 4 — the value "2026" arrives stamped on every record. It is only the master data of the time characteristics (the list of valid values, their texts, their ordering) that is never loaded, because the read class serves it virtually. Compare this with 0MATERIAL or 0CUSTOMER, whose master data is genuinely business-defined and must be loaded from the source via attribute and text DataSources. Time characteristics are the special case where SAP replaced the load with a class.

Stage 5 — What happens at query runtime

The local T009B copy and the read classes come together at query runtime. The OLAP engine consults them whenever fiscal logic is needed: deriving the current fiscal period from today's date for a variable, calculating period offsets (previous period, same period last year), building year-to-date ranges, serving F4 value helps for fiscal years and periods, and sorting periods correctly — including keeping special periods 013–016 in their proper place after period 012. None of this would work if BW treated 0FISCPER as a plain text value; it works because BW knows, from its replicated T009B and its time-characteristic read classes, how periods relate to dates and to each other.

The distinction that matters: source of truth vs consumer

Putting the stages together, the population story becomes very clear. ECC is the single source of truth: the fiscal calendar is populated there once, as Customizing in OB29, and applied millions of times, as period derivation on every posting. BW's fiscal calendar is populated twice over — once as replicated Customizing via Transfer Global Settings (the rulebook), and continuously as already-stamped values on every extracted record (the data). Its time characteristics need no master data load at all, because their read classes generate values from the rules. At no point does BW independently recalculate what ECC decided.

This has a practical consequence: if the variant configuration changes in ECC — a new period arrangement, a shortened fiscal year via T009C, a newly maintained year for a year-dependent variant — BW does not pick it up on its own. The global settings must be re-transferred, and only records loaded afterwards reflect the new rules. So when fiscal periods in BW look wrong, check in this order: was the period maintained in OB29 for the new year, were global settings re-transferred, and is the transformation mapping or deriving the time characteristics as expected. It is almost always one of these three — not a calculation error in BW.

Aspect

ECC

BW

Master config table

T009 (variant), T009B (period dates), maintained via OB29

Local replicated copy of T009/T009B via Transfer Global Settings — used for derivation, never for reporting

Characteristic / field

PERIV, MONAT, GJAHR

0FISCVARNT, 0FISCPER, 0FISCYEAR

Master data load

Not applicable — configuration, not data

None for time characteristics — served virtually by CL_RSMD_RS_* read classes ("Own Implementation")

Role

Source of truth — derives the period at posting time

Consumer — stores fiscal period as a reporting characteristic and derives only via the replicated rulebook

Special periods

Periods 13–16 (adjustment periods) supported in T009B, entered manually at closing

0FISCPER supports adjustment periods as additional period values, sorted after period 012

 

A note on newer stacks

In newer generations — BW/4HANA, or embedded analytics on S/4HANA — the same fiscal calendar is exposed through CDS views such as I_FiscalYearVariant and I_FiscalYearPeriod, rather than through the raw pool tables. The underlying logic is still the familiar T009-based configuration; only the access layer has been modernized.

Wrapping up

So the next time someone asks "where does the fiscal period actually come from, and how does it work in BW?", the answer fits in a few lines: it is born as Customizing in OB29 (T009/T009B, with the year shift doing the heavy lifting for non-calendar years), derived onto every document at posting time, copied into BW as global settings, delivered pre-stamped on every extracted record, re-derived in transformations only when needed — always against BW's local rulebook — and served virtually at query runtime by master data read classes that generate fiscal values from rules instead of loading them. There is no fiscal calendar "load" because the calendar was never data to begin with — it is configuration that every downstream layer consumes, and in BW that principle goes so deep that even the master data is a class, not a table.

If you found this useful, I'd be glad to hear how fiscal year variants are handled in your landscape — especially anyone dealing with year-dependent variants or shortened fiscal years, where the population story gets more interesting.

entry.title: What’s New in the RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench
entry.content:
Each delivery of the RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench brings improvements to the customer experience throughout their RISE with SAP migration journey, focusing on automation, downtime reduction, quality validation, and reduced manual effort.

This post highlights recent deliveries aimed at improving operational efficiency and process improvements, expanding Guided Transition Checks, and enhancing transition procedures.

Dynamic Change of Vault Secrets

Customers general security policies operations might require scheduled credential rotations. If a rotation occurs while a migration is running, mismatches in the affected credentials, such as database passwords, would cause the procedure to fail, requiring manual restart. The Transition Workbench now supports dynamic change of vault secrets mid-process to improve the customer experience and the need to go back in the process and restart a certain step task.

Re-usable Download Folder across Migration Runs

In response to partner feedback, the Transition Workbench now supports reusing the download folder across runs. Downloaded software can be reused to support version control and deliver repeatable, reproducible results in subsequent cycles.

Automated Cleanup of the Intermediate System

Temporary resources on the migration server can now be automatically cleaned up between runs simply by enabling the new dedicated option in the cockpit, removing the need for manual housekeeping steps between attempts.

Auto-restart of the Switch-back Process

If a cancellation occurs in the main cockpit, the system can now automatically restart the switch-back process with a cached parameter, reducing manual recovery steps during interrupted runs.

Database Schema Correctness in the Target System’s DEFAULT.PFL during Switchback

During the switchback procedure, a database schema entry in the target system’s DEFAULT.PFL profile file ensures correctness, preventing schema mismatches when the original system is restored.

Guided Transition Checks: Broader Coverage and Clearer Visibility

Guided Transition Checks (GTC) are ABAP checks incorporated in the Workbench cockpit. They validate key system readiness aspects before, during, and after a transition, enabling potential issues to be identified and resolved early rather than during cutover.

Summary

Across operational improvements, quality checks, security enhancements, these deliveries further advance the direction of automated and guided transitions to RISE with SAP Private Cloud Edition, more intuitive and consistent following the standardized processes. entry.title: RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench: Expanded Migration Approaches
entry.content:
The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench is SAP's tool for managing the migration journey into private cloud environments. It supports multiple migration approaches that are available to customers and partners whether their organization is taking a direct conversion path or moving through intermediate steps before the final transformation.

The latest deliveries are expanding our coverage with new additions and enhanced capabilities, that bring to customers a supported, tooling-driven path toward their cloud journey destination. Specifically, the deliveries cover:

  • SAP HANA Tenant Copy Now Supports Different Source and Target Database Setup Architectures
  • New Migration Approach: Lift & Shift with SUM Database Migration Option to SAP HANA
  • SAP Systems on MS SQL Server Now Have a Supported Path to S/4HANA in the Cloud
  • New Cockpit: Uninstall SAP System or Single Instances
  • What This Means for Your Migration Planning
  • Learn More

SAP HANA Tenant Copy Now Supports Different Source and Target Database Setup Architectures

For customers already running SAP HANA on-premise who have committed to a Lift & Shift approach, SAP HANA Tenant Copy is the supported, downtime optimized option for moving their system into a private cloud environment. It relocates the system with/without a database migration or software conversion - useful when business constraints require getting into the cloud environment before undertaking a broader transformation.

Previously, the HANA architecture of the source system had to match the target, therefore a scale-up deployment on-premise required a scale-up target in the cloud.

The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench now supports SAP HANA Tenant Copy across all relevant architecture combinations:

  • Scale-out → Scale-out - move a distributed HANA deployment with multiple nodes to multi-node setup in the RISE with SAP private cloud environment
  • Scale-up → Scale-out - transition from a single large on-premise node  to a distributed SAP HANA architecture in the cloud
  • Scale-out → Scale-up - consolidate a distributed on-premise node onto a single SAP HANA node in the cloud

Customers planning a Lift & Shift approach now have the option to execute those steps using the Transition Workbench — regardless of how source and target SAP HANA architectures differ.

New Migration Approach: Lift & Shift with SUM Database Migration Option to SAP HANA

Customers whose systems still run on a non-HANA database have a new, consolidated option available through the RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench — Lift & Shift with SUM Database Migration Option (DMO) to SAP HANA.

DMO with System Move combines the database migration to SAP HANA and the relocation to the RISE with SAP private cloud environment into a single procedure. The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench guides partners through the required steps from preparation to execution while the SUM-driven migration itself is performed by the partner. Customers who need to move to the cloud before they can plan or execute a full S/4HANA conversion can use this approach to arrive in the cloud already running on HANA, putting them in a significantly better position for the next step of their transformation journey to the Autonomous Enterprise.

SAP Systems on MS SQL Server Now Have a Supported Path to S/4HANA in the Cloud

Customers running SAP systems on Microsoft SQL Server on Windows have a new supported option available through the RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench. The Transition Workbench now supports the DMOVE2S4 against MS SQL based source system conversion approach.

DMOVE2S4 is a SUM-based procedure that converts the source system to S/4HANA and relocates the system to the RISE with SAP private cloud environment - all within a single guided procedure orchestrated through the Transition Workbench.

For this customer segment, the result is a supported, direct path from an MS SQL-based SAP system to the intended destination - S/4HANA in a private cloud environment, eliminating the prerequisite for an infrastructure re-platforming step.

New Cockpit: Uninstall SAP System or Single Instances

Migration procedures leave behind intermediate systems on the Migration VM - temporary installations that served their purpose during the transition but need to be cleanly removed once the migration is complete. The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench now includes a dedicated cockpit for this Uninstall SAP System or Single Instances.

The cockpit uses Software Provisioning Manager (SWPM) to consistently remove an SAP system or selected instances from the Migration VM. It is orchestrated directly through the Transition Workbench, supporting the migration lifecycle, including cleanup - within a single, guided tooling experience.

The process is divided into two steps - downloading the correct version of SWPM and executing the uninstallation. Parameters entered during the procedure are cached and reused across steps, reducing repetition. For scenarios where the /sapmnt directory is mounted from the source SAP system, the cockpit enforces selective instance removal rather than a full system uninstall - preventing unintended changes to source system data.

This addition means customers and partners no longer need to handle post-migration cleanup outside of the Transition Workbench. The intermediate system removal is now a supported, tooling-driven step within the same process.

What This Means for Your Migration Planning

These enhancements expand the range of supported options to transition to a private cloud environment with automated procedures within the Transition Workbench. More customers and partners can now start or continue their journey with a tooling-driven, supported process - reducing manual effort and lowering risk at every stage.

The RISE with SAP System Transition Workbench is available for free, pre-installed and pre-configured as part of your RISE environment.

entry.title: Automating SAP AFO & BW Query Documentation at Scale for Self-Service
entry.content:
Every SAP BW developer knows the drill. A business user pings you: "How is Net Sales actually calculated in this report?" So you open the query in Query Designer, squint through nested formulas, restricted key figures, and condition filters, and piece together an answer — for one query. Now multiply that by hundreds or thousands of queries across the landscape. That is the wall we kept hitting, and this post is the story of how we turned that documentation burden into an AI-powered, self-service knowledge base.

Introduction & Motivation

Documenting SAP Analysis for Office (AFO) and BEx/BW queries at scale is a familiar headache for data engineering teams. A single enterprise reporting query carries dense business logic and metadata:

  • Dynamic Time Columns: Current Period, Prior Year, YTD, MTD, Formulas and CKFs etc.
  • Complex Row Structures: Formulas for Gross Sales, Deductions, Net Sales, Contribution Margin, and Operating Profit.
  • Restricted Key Figures (RKFs): Dozens of restricted metrics with layered condition filters.
  • Free Characteristics: Dynamic drilldown attributes and dimensions.

Doing this by hand across hundreds or thousands of queries is slow, inconsistent, and nearly impossible to keep current.

The Problem: The "Mass Execution" Bottleneck

The standard query-definition tool (program RSRQ_QUERYDEFINITION, transaction RSRTQ) is built to extract and display the internal elements of AFO/BW queries. It captures almost everything a developer or functional analyst needs. However, downloading a single query definition was never the true problem. The real challenge was mass execution and consumption:

  • How do you generate standardized design documents for thousands of queries at once without manual execution?
  • How do you feed that generated metadata into a central AI chatbot agent so end-users can self-serve?

Instead of an analyst digging through static PDF or Word exports to figure out how a metric is calculated, we wanted users to ask our chatbot in plain language:

"Which query should I use for region-wise margin analysis, and what is the exact formula behind Net Sales? What is its Formula ?"

[The starting point: RSRQ_QUERYDEFINITION selection screen for a single query, and its exported output. : the standard tool documents one query at a time.]

The Architecture: From Raw Query to AI Q&A

Rather than authoring documents manually, we treat documentation as a generated artifact.

The data flows through five stages, each feeding the next:

SAP BW Query Landscape 

⬇

Mass Extract (ABAP Generator) Structured Metadata Engine

⬇

Format (.docx / Standard Template) Central Document Repository (Single Source of Truth) 

⬇

Crawl & Index (RAG Engine) AI Knowledge Assistant (Eg. CoPilot)→ Natural Language Self-Service

You can also read it as a single left-to-right pipeline:

Query Landscape → Metadata Engine → Document Repository → AI Assistant → Self-Service Q&A

The 5-Step Pipeline

  1. Extract: An automated program reads query definitions from standard SAP metadata tables and APIs at mass.
  2. Format: The extracted metadata is dynamically rendered into standardized technical design documents using a unified team template.     Program output: a generated technical design document showing columns, row formulas restricted key figures, and free characteristics in the standard template.
  3. Publish: The generated documents land automatically in a central, governed document repository.
  4. Index: An enterprise search platform / RAG crawler ingests and chunks the standardized documents.
  5. Serve: An AI knowledge assistant answers user questions, fully grounded in actual technical design logic.

AI self-service: the chatbot answering "what is the formula behind Avg. Delivery?" with the response grounded in the generated documentation

 Shift in Paradigm: Manual vs. Automated

Aspect

Manual Approach

Automated Approach

Workflow

Query → Manual Read → Hand-written Doc → Local Drive

Query → Mass Generator → Central Repo → AI Search

Effort

High (hours per query)

Minimal (run on demand/transport)

Consistency

Low (varies by analyst style)

100% enforced standardization

Searchability

Keyword hunting in random folders

Natural-language chatbot Q&A

Governance

Ad hoc & scattered

Governed single source of truth

Closing Thoughts

If the underlying SAP artifact is already structured, don't write the documentation — generate it. By building a mass extraction pipeline and connecting it to an enterprise AI layer, you turn passive metadata into an active self-service knowledge base.
  • Delta Metadata Freshness: Tracking "Created On" and "Last Changed On" dates on the program enables scheduling of delta query change extraction, so the AI reindexes only modified queries.
  • Automated Governance: Post-transport background scheduling captures timestamped changes, maintaining an always up-to-date, audit-ready single source of truth.
  • True Self-Service: Eliminating manual effort provides business users with instant, AI-powered answers while freeing developers to focus on core tasks.

Program summary: This program is a bare-minimum build created for our own needs, providing Info about Query Structure Formula, RKF, CKF, etc. Both the generation logic and the self-service layer can be modified to fit your required needs. The crux lies behind the function module RSZ_DB_ELT_GET, which reads the query element definitions (columns, rows, restricted key figures, free characteristics, and formulas) that everything else is built on.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Report ZBW_QUERY_DEF_EXPORTER
*& Technical Documentation Exporter for BW Queries (Complete & Modular)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
REPORT zbw_query_def_exporter.

INCLUDE rsrq_querydefinition_dat.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Selection Screen
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b1 WITH FRAME TITLE title1.
  SELECT-OPTIONS: s_compid FOR rsrrepdir-compid,
                  s_infocb FOR rsrrepdir-infocube.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b1.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b3 WITH FRAME TITLE title2.
  PARAMETERS: rb_crt RADIOBUTTON GROUP rg1 DEFAULT 'X' USER-COMMAND rad,
              rb_chg RADIOBUTTON GROUP rg1.
  SELECT-OPTIONS: s_date FOR sy-datum NO INTERVALS NO-EXTENSION.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b3.

SELECTION-SCREEN BEGIN OF BLOCK b2 WITH FRAME TITLE title3.
  PARAMETERS: p_path TYPE string LOWER CASE OBLIGATORY.
SELECTION-SCREEN END OF BLOCK b2.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Data Declarations
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_query,
         compid   TYPE rsrrepdir-compid,
         infocube TYPE rsrrepdir-infocube,
         compuid  TYPE rsrrepdir-compuid,
         genuniid TYPE rsrrepdir-genuniid,
         objvers  TYPE rsrrepdir-objvers,
         tstpnm   TYPE rszcompdir-tstpnm,
         tstpdat  TYPE rszcompdir-tstpdat,
         tstptim  TYPE rszcompdir-tstptim,
         created  TYPE rszcompdir-created,
         lastused TYPE rszcompdir-lastused,
       END OF ty_query.

TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_axis_item,
         axis_type TYPE string,
         posn      TYPE i,
         eltuid    TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid,
         tech_name TYPE string,
         desc_text TYPE string,
         elem_type TYPE string,
       END OF ty_axis_item.

TYPES tt_axis_item TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_axis_item WITH DEFAULT KEY.
TYPES tt_rszcalc   TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF rszcalc WITH DEFAULT KEY.

DATA: gt_queries  TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_query,
      gw_query    TYPE ty_query,
      gv_sep      TYPE c,
      gv_filename TYPE string,
      gv_fullpath TYPE string,
      gt_text_doc TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string.

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Initialization & Selection Screen Events
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
INITIALIZATION.
  title1 = 'Query Selection Criteria'.
  title2 = 'Date Filter Criteria'.
  title3 = 'Target Export Directory'.
  cl_gui_frontend_services=>get_desktop_directory(
    CHANGING desktop_directory = p_path
    EXCEPTIONS OTHERS = 1 ).
  cl_gui_cfw=>flush( ).

AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.
  %_s_compid_%_app_%-text = 'Query Technical Name'.
  %_s_infocb_%_app_%-text = 'InfoProvider / Cube'.
  %_rb_crt_%_app_%-text   = 'Filter by Created Date'.
  %_rb_chg_%_app_%-text   = 'Filter by Last Changed Date'.
  %_s_date_%_app_%-text   = 'Select Date'.
  %_p_path_%_app_%-text   = 'Target Folder Path'.

AT SELECTION-SCREEN ON VALUE-REQUEST FOR p_path.
  cl_gui_frontend_services=>directory_browse(
    EXPORTING window_title   = 'Select Target Folder'
              initial_folder = p_path
    CHANGING  selected_folder = p_path
    EXCEPTIONS OTHERS = 1 ).

*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
* Main Processing Logic
*----------------------------------------------------------------------*
START-OF-SELECTION.

  IF rb_crt = 'X'.
    DATA: lt_created_range TYPE RANGE OF rszcompdir-created,
          ls_created_range LIKE LINE OF lt_created_range.

    LOOP AT s_date INTO DATA(ls_date).
      CLEAR ls_created_range.
      ls_created_range-sign   = ls_date-sign.
      ls_created_range-option = ls_date-option.
      ls_created_range-low    = |{ ls_date-low }000000|.
      ls_created_range-high   = COND #( WHEN ls_date-high IS NOT INITIAL
                                        THEN |{ ls_date-high }235959|
                                        ELSE |{ ls_date-low }235959| ).
      APPEND ls_created_range TO lt_created_range.
    ENDLOOP.

    SELECT a~compid, a~infocube, a~compuid, a~genuniid, a~objvers,
           b~tstpnm, b~tstpdat, b~tstptim, b~created, b~lastused
      FROM rsrrepdir AS a
      INNER JOIN rszcompdir AS b
        ON a~compuid = b~compuid
      INTO TABLE @gt_queries
      WHERE a~objvers  = 'A'
        AND a~comptype = 'REP'
        AND a~compid   IN @s_compid
        AND a~infocube IN @s_infocb
        AND b~objvers  = 'A'
        AND b~created  IN @LT_created_range.
  ELSE.
    SELECT a~compid, a~infocube, a~compuid, a~genuniid, a~objvers,
           b~tstpnm, b~tstpdat, b~tstptim, b~created, b~lastused
      FROM rsrrepdir AS a
      INNER JOIN rszcompdir AS b
        ON a~compuid = b~compuid
      INTO TABLE @gt_queries
      WHERE a~objvers  = 'A'
        AND a~comptype = 'REP'
        AND a~compid   IN @s_compid
        AND a~infocube IN @s_infocb
        AND b~objvers  = 'A'
        AND b~tstpdat  IN @s_date.
  ENDIF.

  IF gt_queries IS INITIAL.
    MESSAGE 'No active queries found matching selection criteria.' TYPE 'I'.
    LEAVE TO SCREEN 0.
  ENDIF.

  cl_gui_frontend_services=>get_file_separator(
    CHANGING file_separator = gv_sep
    EXCEPTIONS OTHERS = 1 ).

  IF p_path IS NOT INITIAL
     AND substring( val = p_path off = strlen( p_path ) - 1 len = 1 ) <> gv_sep.
    p_path = p_path && gv_sep.
  ENDIF.

  DATA(lv_total_queries) = lines( gt_queries ).
  DATA(lv_current_index) = 0.

  LOOP AT gt_queries INTO gw_query.
    lv_current_index = lv_current_index + 1.

    DATA(lv_percent) = ( lv_current_index * 100 ) / lv_total_queries.
    DATA(lv_text)    = |Processing query { lv_current_index }/{ lv_total_queries }: { gw_query-compid }|.

    CALL FUNCTION 'SAPGUI_PROGRESS_INDICATOR'
      EXPORTING
        percentage = lv_percent
        text       = lv_text.

    PERFORM process_single_query USING gw_query.
  ENDLOOP.

  ULINE.
  WRITE: / 'Mass export completed. Target directory:', p_path.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: PROCESS_SINGLE_QUERY
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM process_single_query USING is_query TYPE ty_query.

  CLEAR: g_s_rkb1d, gv_filename, gv_fullpath.

  REFRESH: gt_text_doc, g_th_eltdir, g_th_elttxt, g_th_eltprop,
           g_th_eltprio, g_th_eltattr, g_th_eltxref, g_th_compdir,
           g_th_compic, g_th_changes, g_th_select, g_th_range,
           g_th_calc, g_th_cel, g_th_globv, g_th_missing_elements,
           g_th_compext.

  SELECT SINGLE *
    FROM rsrrepdir
    INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF g_s_rkb1d
    WHERE genuniid = is_query-genuniid
      AND objvers  = is_query-objvers.

  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  CALL FUNCTION 'RSZ_DB_ELT_GET'
    EXPORTING
      i_infocube            = g_s_rkb1d-infocube
      i_eltuid              = g_s_rkb1d-compuid
    IMPORTING
      e_th_eltdir           = g_th_eltdir
      e_th_elttxt           = g_th_elttxt
      e_th_eltprop          = g_th_eltprop
      e_th_eltprio          = g_th_eltprio
      e_th_eltattr          = g_th_eltattr
      e_th_eltxref          = g_th_eltxref
      e_th_compdir          = g_th_compdir
      e_th_compic           = g_th_compic
      e_th_changes          = g_th_changes
      e_th_select           = g_th_select
      e_th_range            = g_th_range
      e_th_calc             = g_th_calc
      e_th_cel              = g_th_cel
      e_th_globv            = g_th_globv
      e_th_missing_elements = g_th_missing_elements
      e_backup_exists       = g_backup_exists
      e_th_compext          = g_th_compext
    EXCEPTIONS
      OTHERS = 1.

  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    WRITE: / 'Error reading elements for query:', is_query-compid.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  PERFORM build_rtf_document CHANGING gt_text_doc.

  DATA(lv_raw_desc) = CONV string( is_query-compid ).
  READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_qdesc>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = g_s_rkb1d-compuid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_qdesc>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
    lv_raw_desc = <fs_qdesc>-txtlg.
  ENDIF.

  DATA(lv_safe_compid) = REPLACE( val = is_query-compid sub = '/' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_compid       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_compid sub = '\' with = '_' occ = 0 ).

  DATA(lv_safe_desc) = REPLACE( val = lv_raw_desc sub = '/' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '\' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = ':' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '*' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '?' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '"' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '<' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '>' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  lv_safe_desc       = REPLACE( val = lv_safe_desc sub = '|' with = '_' occ = 0 ).
  CONDENSE lv_safe_desc.

  gv_filename = |{ lv_safe_compid }_{ lv_safe_desc }.doc|.
  gv_fullpath = |{ p_path }{ gv_filename }|.

  CALL FUNCTION 'GUI_DOWNLOAD'
    EXPORTING
      filename             = gv_fullpath
      filetype             = 'ASC'
      no_auth_check        = 'X'
      show_transfer_status = space
    TABLES
      data_tab             = gt_text_doc
    EXCEPTIONS
      OTHERS = 1.

  IF sy-subrc = 0.
    WRITE: / 'Successfully exported document:', gv_filename.
  ELSE.
    WRITE: / 'Error exporting document for query:', is_query-compid.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: BUILD_RTF_DOCUMENT
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM build_rtf_document CHANGING ct_doc TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

  DATA lv_query_desc(60) TYPE c.

  READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_qdesc>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = g_s_rkb1d-compuid.

  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_qdesc>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
    lv_query_desc = <fs_qdesc>-txtlg.
  ELSE.
    lv_query_desc = g_s_rkb1d-compid.
  ENDIF.

  PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_query_desc.

  APPEND '{\rtf1\ansi\deff0{\fonttbl{\f0 Arial;}{\f1 Courier New;}}{\colortbl;\red235\green238\blue242;}' TO ct_doc.

  PERFORM build_header_section CHANGING ct_doc.
  PERFORM build_axis_sections CHANGING ct_doc.
  PERFORM build_variables_section CHANGING ct_doc.
  PERFORM build_filters_section CHANGING ct_doc.
  PERFORM build_formulas_appendix CHANGING ct_doc.

  APPEND '}' TO ct_doc.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: BUILD_HEADER_SECTION
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM build_header_section CHANGING ct_doc TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

  DATA: lv_created_on TYPE string,
        lv_changed_on TYPE string,
        lv_owner      TYPE rsrrepdir-author,
        lv_lastuser   TYPE rsrrepdir-lastuser,
        lv_gentime    TYPE rsrrepdir-gentime.

  SELECT SINGLE author, lastuser, gentime
    FROM rsrrepdir
    INTO (@lv_owner, @LV_lastuser, @LV_gentime)
    WHERE genuniid = @G_S_rkb1d-genuniid
      AND objvers  = @G_S_rkb1d-objvers.

  lv_created_on = COND #( WHEN lv_owner IS NOT INITIAL
                          THEN lv_owner
                          ELSE 'N/A' ).

  IF lv_gentime IS NOT INITIAL.
    DATA(lv_tstr) = CONV string( lv_gentime ).

    IF strlen( lv_tstr ) >= 8.
      lv_changed_on = |{ lv_tstr(4) }-{ lv_tstr+4(2) }-{ lv_tstr+6(2) } by { lv_lastuser }|.
    ELSE.
      lv_changed_on = |by { lv_lastuser }|.
    ENDIF.
  ELSE.
    lv_changed_on = |by { lv_lastuser }|.
  ENDIF.

  DATA(lv_query_desc) = g_s_rkb1d-compid.

  READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_qdesc>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = g_s_rkb1d-compuid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_qdesc>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
    lv_query_desc = <fs_qdesc>-txtlg.
  ENDIF.

  PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_query_desc.

  APPEND '\viewkind4\uc1\pard\f0\fs24\b TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION FOR BW QUERY\b0\par' TO ct_doc.
  APPEND '\line' TO ct_doc.
  APPEND |\\f0\\fs20\\b Query Description:\\b0 { lv_query_desc }\\par| TO ct_doc.
  APPEND |\\b Technical Name:\\b0   { g_s_rkb1d-compid }\\par| TO ct_doc.
  APPEND |\\b InfoProvider:\\b0      { g_s_rkb1d-infocube }\\par| TO ct_doc.
  APPEND |\\b Created By:\\b0        { lv_created_on }\\par| TO ct_doc.
  APPEND |\\b Last Changed On:\\b0  { lv_changed_on }\\par| TO ct_doc.
  APPEND '\line' TO ct_doc.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: BUILD_AXIS_SECTIONS (Modular Coordinator)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM build_axis_sections CHANGING ct_doc TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

  DATA: lt_col_items  TYPE tt_axis_item,
        lt_row_items  TYPE tt_axis_item,
        lt_free_items TYPE tt_axis_item.

  " 1. Extract each axis independently
  PERFORM extract_columns_axis CHANGING lt_col_items.
  PERFORM extract_rows_axis    CHANGING lt_row_items.
  PERFORM extract_free_chars   CHANGING lt_free_items.

  " 2. Render each axis table
  PERFORM render_axis_table
    USING    '1. Columns Axis (COL)' 'COL' lt_col_items
    CHANGING ct_doc.

  PERFORM render_axis_table
    USING    '2. Rows Axis (ROW)' 'ROW' lt_row_items
    CHANGING ct_doc.

  PERFORM render_axis_table
    USING    '3. Free Characteristics (AGR)' 'AGR' lt_free_items
    CHANGING ct_doc.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: EXTRACT_COLUMNS_AXIS
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM extract_columns_axis CHANGING ct_col_items TYPE tt_axis_item.

  PERFORM extract_axis_items
    USING    rzd1_c_laytp-column 'COL'
    CHANGING ct_col_items.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: EXTRACT_ROWS_AXIS
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM extract_rows_axis CHANGING ct_row_items TYPE tt_axis_item.

  PERFORM extract_axis_items
    USING    rzd1_c_laytp-row 'ROW'
    CHANGING ct_row_items.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: EXTRACT_FREE_CHARS
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM extract_free_chars CHANGING ct_free_items TYPE tt_axis_item.

  PERFORM extract_axis_items
    USING    rzd1_c_laytp-aggregated 'AGR'
    CHANGING ct_free_items.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: EXTRACT_AXIS_ITEMS (Generic Unnester for Given Laytp)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM extract_axis_items USING    VALUE(iv_laytp) TYPE any
                                 iv_axis_code    TYPE string
                        CHANGING ct_axis_items   TYPE tt_axis_item.

  DATA: ls_axis       TYPE ty_axis_item,
        lt_child_xref TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF rzd1_s_eltxref,
        ls_child_xref TYPE rzd1_s_eltxref.

  CLEAR ct_axis_items.

  LOOP AT g_th_eltxref ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_xref>)
       WHERE laytp = iv_laytp.

    READ TABLE g_th_eltdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_dir>)
         WITH KEY eltuid = <fs_xref>-teltuid.

    " Structure expansion
    IF <fs_dir> IS ASSIGNED AND ( <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-structure OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-structure ).

      REFRESH lt_child_xref.
      LOOP AT g_th_eltxref INTO ls_child_xref
           WHERE seltuid = <fs_xref>-teltuid.
        APPEND ls_child_xref TO lt_child_xref.
      ENDLOOP.

      SORT lt_child_xref BY posn.

      LOOP AT lt_child_xref INTO ls_child_xref.
        CLEAR ls_axis.
        ls_axis-axis_type = iv_axis_code.
        ls_axis-posn      = ls_child_xref-posn.
        ls_axis-eltuid    = ls_child_xref-teltuid.

        PERFORM resolve_generic_element
          USING    ls_child_xref-teltuid
          CHANGING ls_axis-desc_text ls_axis-tech_name ls_axis-elem_type.

        IF ls_axis-desc_text IS NOT INITIAL OR ls_axis-tech_name IS NOT INITIAL.
          PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING ls_axis-desc_text.
          APPEND ls_axis TO ct_axis_items.
        ENDIF.
      ENDLOOP.

    ELSE.

      CLEAR ls_axis.
      ls_axis-axis_type = iv_axis_code.
      ls_axis-posn      = <fs_xref>-posn.
      ls_axis-eltuid    = <fs_xref>-teltuid.

      PERFORM resolve_generic_element
        USING    <fs_xref>-teltuid
        CHANGING ls_axis-desc_text ls_axis-tech_name ls_axis-elem_type.

      IF ls_axis-desc_text IS NOT INITIAL OR ls_axis-tech_name IS NOT INITIAL.
        PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING ls_axis-desc_text.
        APPEND ls_axis TO ct_axis_items.
      ENDIF.

    ENDIF.

  ENDLOOP.

  SORT ct_axis_items BY axis_type eltuid posn.
  DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM ct_axis_items COMPARING axis_type eltuid.
  SORT ct_axis_items BY axis_type posn eltuid.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RESOLVE_GENERIC_ELEMENT (Core Element Resolver)
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM resolve_generic_element USING    VALUE(i_uid) TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                             CHANGING cv_desc      TYPE string
                                      cv_tech      TYPE string
                                      cv_elem_type TYPE string.

  DATA: lv_is_formula   TYPE abap_bool,
        lv_is_selection TYPE abap_bool,
        lv_is_char      TYPE abap_bool,
        lv_is_struct    TYPE abap_bool,
        lv_target_uid   TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid.

  CLEAR: cv_desc, cv_tech, cv_elem_type.
  lv_target_uid = i_uid.

  " 1. Detect Metadata Category and resolve Reusable Target UIDs
  PERFORM determine_element_metadata
    USING    i_uid
    CHANGING lv_target_uid
             lv_is_formula
             lv_is_selection
             lv_is_char
             lv_is_struct.

  " 2. Resolve Global Reusable Technical Name from RSZCOMPDIR
  PERFORM get_global_component_id
    USING    lv_target_uid
    CHANGING cv_tech.

  " 3. Pure Characteristic InfoObject Fallback
  IF cv_tech IS INITIAL AND lv_is_char = abap_true.
    PERFORM get_infoobject_techname
      USING    lv_target_uid
      CHANGING cv_tech.
  ENDIF.

  " 4. Element Type & Technical Name Assignment
  IF cv_tech IS INITIAL OR cv_tech = lv_target_uid.
    cv_tech = lv_target_uid.
    IF lv_is_formula = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'Local Formula'.
    ELSEIF lv_is_selection = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'Local Selection'.
    ELSEIF lv_is_char = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'Characteristic'.
    ELSEIF lv_is_struct = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'Structure'.
    ELSE.
      cv_elem_type = 'Local Selection'.
    ENDIF.
  ELSE.
    IF lv_is_formula = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'CKF'.
    ELSEIF lv_is_selection = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'RKF'.
    ELSEIF lv_is_char = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'Characteristic'.
    ELSEIF lv_is_struct = abap_true.
      cv_elem_type = 'Structure'.
    ELSE.
      cv_elem_type = 'Element'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  " 5. Description Resolution (Never substituting cv_tech with description)
  PERFORM resolve_element_description
    USING    i_uid lv_target_uid cv_elem_type cv_tech
    CHANGING cv_desc.

  IF cv_desc IS INITIAL.
    cv_desc = cv_tech.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: DETERMINE_ELEMENT_METADATA
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM determine_element_metadata USING    VALUE(i_uid)     TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                                CHANGING cv_target_uid   TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                                         cv_is_formula   TYPE abap_bool
                                         cv_is_selection TYPE abap_bool
                                         cv_is_char      TYPE abap_bool
                                         cv_is_struct    TYPE abap_bool.

  CLEAR: cv_is_formula, cv_is_selection, cv_is_char, cv_is_struct.
  cv_target_uid = i_uid.

  READ TABLE g_th_eltdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_dir>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = i_uid.

  " 1. Strict Formula Detection on i_uid
  IF <fs_dir> IS ASSIGNED AND ( <fs_dir>-deftp = 'FML' OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = 'FML'
                             OR <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-formula OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-formula
                             OR <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-calkeyfig OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-calkeyfig ).
    cv_is_formula = abap_true.
  ELSE.
    READ TABLE g_th_calc WITH KEY eltuid = i_uid TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      cv_is_formula = abap_true.
    ELSE.
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rszcalc WHERE eltuid = i_uid AND objvers = 'A'.
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        cv_is_formula = abap_true.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  " 2. Reusable Element Unwrapping for Selections only (strictly checking SUBDEFTP = 'RKF'/'CKF')
  " Variables (DEFTP = 'VAR') MUST NOT be unwrapped!
  IF cv_is_formula = abap_false AND <fs_dir> IS ASSIGNED AND <fs_dir>-subdeftp = 'STM'.
    READ TABLE g_th_eltxref ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_xref>)
         WITH KEY seltuid = i_uid.
    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_xref>-teltuid IS NOT INITIAL.
      READ TABLE g_th_eltdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_target_dir>)
           WITH KEY eltuid = <fs_xref>-teltuid.
      IF sy-subrc = 0 AND ( <fs_target_dir>-subdeftp = 'RKF' OR <fs_target_dir>-subdeftp = 'CKF' )
                      AND <fs_target_dir>-deftp <> 'VAR'.
        cv_target_uid = <fs_xref>-teltuid.
        ASSIGN <fs_target_dir> TO <fs_dir>.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  " 3. Classify non-formula types
  IF cv_is_formula = abap_false AND <fs_dir> IS ASSIGNED.
    IF <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-structure OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-structure.
      cv_is_struct = abap_true.
    ELSEIF <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-characteristic OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-characteristic
        OR ( <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-selection AND <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-characteristic ).
      cv_is_char = abap_true.
    ELSEIF <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-formula OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-formula
        OR <fs_dir>-deftp = rzd1_c_deftp-calkeyfig OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-calkeyfig
        OR <fs_dir>-deftp = 'FML' OR <fs_dir>-subdeftp = 'FML'.
      cv_is_formula = abap_true.
    ELSE.
      cv_is_selection = abap_true.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: GET_GLOBAL_COMPONENT_ID
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM get_global_component_id USING    VALUE(iv_uid) TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                             CHANGING cv_tech       TYPE string.

  CLEAR cv_tech.

  READ TABLE g_th_compdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_cdir>) WITH KEY compuid = iv_uid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_cdir>-compid IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_tech = <fs_cdir>-compid.
  ELSE.
    SELECT SINGLE compid
      FROM rszcompdir
      INTO @CV_tech
      WHERE compuid = @iv_uid
        AND objvers = 'A'.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: GET_INFOOBJECT_TECHNAME
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM get_infoobject_techname USING    VALUE(iv_uid) TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                             CHANGING cv_tech       TYPE string.

  CLEAR cv_tech.

  READ TABLE g_th_select ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_sel>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = iv_uid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_sel>-iobjnm IS NOT INITIAL AND <fs_sel>-iobjnm <> '1KYFNM' AND <fs_sel>-iobjnm <> '1'.
    cv_tech = <fs_sel>-iobjnm.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RESOLVE_ELEMENT_DESCRIPTION
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM resolve_element_description USING    VALUE(iv_uid)        TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                                          VALUE(iv_target_uid) TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                                          VALUE(iv_elem_type)  TYPE string
                                          VALUE(iv_tech)       TYPE string
                                 CHANGING cv_desc              TYPE string.

  CLEAR cv_desc.

  READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_txt>) WITH KEY eltuid = iv_uid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_txt>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_desc = <fs_txt>-txtlg.
  ELSE.
    READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING <fs_txt> WITH KEY eltuid = iv_target_uid.
    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_txt>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
      cv_desc = <fs_txt>-txtlg.
    ELSE.
      READ TABLE g_th_eltdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_dir>) WITH KEY eltuid = iv_uid.
      IF <fs_dir> IS ASSIGNED AND <fs_dir>-defaulthint IS NOT INITIAL.
        PERFORM resolve_defaulthint USING <fs_dir>-defaulthint CHANGING cv_desc.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  PERFORM resolve_text_variables CHANGING cv_desc.

  IF cv_desc IS INITIAL AND iv_elem_type = 'Characteristic' AND iv_tech <> iv_target_uid.
    SELECT SINGLE txtlg FROM rsdiobjt INTO @DATA(lv_iobj_txt)
      WHERE iobjnm = @iv_tech AND langu = @SY-langu AND objvers = 'A'.
    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND lv_iobj_txt IS NOT INITIAL.
      cv_desc = lv_iobj_txt.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: BUILD_FILTERS_SECTION
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM build_filters_section CHANGING ct_doc TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

  DATA: lt_rkf_eltuids TYPE HASHED TABLE OF rszeltdir-eltuid
                            WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
        lv_found       TYPE abap_bool VALUE abap_false,
        lv_filter_val  TYPE string.

  APPEND '{\f0\fs22\b 5. Selection Ranges & Filter Conditions (G_TH_RANGE)\b0\par}' TO ct_doc.

  IF g_th_range IS INITIAL.
    APPEND '{\f1\fs18  No explicit global range restrictions defined.\par}\par' TO ct_doc.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  LOOP AT g_th_range ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_rkf_chk>)
       WHERE iobjnm = '1KYFNM'.
    INSERT <fs_rkf_chk>-eltuid INTO TABLE lt_rkf_eltuids.
  ENDLOOP.

  LOOP AT g_th_range ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_rng>).

    IF <fs_rng>-iobjnm = '1KYFNM'.
      CONTINUE.
    ENDIF.

    IF lt_rkf_eltuids IS NOT INITIAL.
      READ TABLE lt_rkf_eltuids
           WITH KEY table_line = <fs_rng>-eltuid
           TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.

      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    CLEAR lv_filter_val.

    PERFORM resolve_filter_value
      USING    <fs_rng>-low
      CHANGING lv_filter_val.

    IF lv_filter_val IS INITIAL.
      CONTINUE.
    ENDIF.

    IF lv_found = abap_false.
      lv_found = abap_true.

      DATA(lv_hdr) = '\trowd\trgaph108\trleft360' &&
                     '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\clcbpat1\cellx3500' &&
                     '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\clcbpat1\cellx4800' &&
                     '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\clcbpat1\cellx6000' &&
                     '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\clcbpat1\cellx10000' &&
                     '\param\f1\fs18 Field / InfoObject\cell Sign\cell Operator\cell Filter Value\cell\row\intbl'.

      APPEND lv_hdr TO ct_doc.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_iobj) = COND string( WHEN <fs_rng>-iobjnm IS NOT INITIAL
                                 THEN <fs_rng>-iobjnm ELSE '-' ).
    DATA(lv_sign) = COND string( WHEN <fs_rng>-sign IS NOT INITIAL
                                 THEN <fs_rng>-sign ELSE 'I' ).
    DATA(lv_opt)  = COND string( WHEN <fs_rng>-opt IS NOT INITIAL
                                 THEN <fs_rng>-opt ELSE 'EQ' ).

    PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_filter_val.

    DATA(lv_row) = '\trowd\trgaph108\trleft360' &&
                   '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\cellx3500' &&
                   '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\cellx4800' &&
                   '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\cellx6000' &&
                   '\clbrdrt\brdrs\clbrdrl\brdrs\clbrdrb\brdrs\clbrdrr\brdrs\cellx10000' &&
                   |\\param\\f1\\fs18 { lv_iobj }\\cell { lv_sign }\\cell { lv_opt }\\cell { lv_filter_val }\\cell\\row\\intbl|.

    APPEND lv_row TO ct_doc.

  ENDLOOP.

  IF lv_found = abap_false.
    APPEND '{\f1\fs18  No explicit global range restrictions defined.\par}\par' TO ct_doc.
  ELSE.
    APPEND '\pard\par' TO ct_doc.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: BUILD_FORMULAS_APPENDIX
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM build_formulas_appendix CHANGING ct_doc TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

  DATA: lv_count     TYPE i VALUE 0,
        lv_formula   TYPE string,
        lv_aggr_type TYPE string,
        lv_disp_name TYPE string,
        lv_line      TYPE string.

  APPEND '\f0\fs22\b 6. Appendix: RKF / CKF / Local Selections & Formulas Tree Diagnostics\b0\par' TO ct_doc.
  APPEND '{\f1\fs18' TO ct_doc.

  LOOP AT g_th_eltdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_dir>)
       WHERE deftp    = rzd1_c_deftp-calkeyfig
          OR deftp    = rzd1_c_deftp-restkeyfig
          OR deftp    = rzd1_c_deftp-selection
          OR deftp    = rzd1_c_deftp-formula
          OR deftp    = 'FML'
          OR subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-calkeyfig
          OR subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-restkeyfig
          OR subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-selection
          OR subdeftp = rzd1_c_deftp-formula
          OR subdeftp = 'FML'.

    READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_txt>)
         WITH KEY eltuid = <fs_dir>-eltuid.

    DATA(lv_desc) = COND string(
      WHEN sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_txt>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL
        THEN <fs_txt>-txtlg
        ELSE '' ).

    IF lv_desc IS INITIAL AND <fs_dir>-defaulthint IS NOT INITIAL.
      PERFORM resolve_defaulthint USING <fs_dir>-defaulthint CHANGING lv_desc.
    ENDIF.

    PERFORM resolve_text_variables CHANGING lv_desc.

    CLEAR lv_disp_name.
    READ TABLE g_th_compdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_cdir>) WITH KEY compuid = <fs_dir>-eltuid.
    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_cdir>-compid IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_disp_name = <fs_cdir>-compid.
    ELSE.
      SELECT SINGLE compid
        FROM rszcompdir
        INTO @LV_disp_name
        WHERE compuid = @<fs_dir>-eltuid
          AND objvers = 'A'.
    ENDIF.

    IF lv_disp_name IS INITIAL.
      lv_disp_name = <fs_dir>-eltuid.
    ENDIF.

    CLEAR lv_formula.
    PERFORM reconstruct_formula_tree
      USING    <fs_dir>-eltuid
      CHANGING lv_formula.

    DATA(lv_has_filters) = abap_false.
    LOOP AT g_th_range ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_rng_chk>)
              WHERE eltuid = <fs_dir>-eltuid.
      lv_has_filters = abap_true.
      EXIT.
    ENDLOOP.

    DATA(lv_has_calc) = abap_false.
    READ TABLE g_th_calc ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_calc>)
         WITH KEY eltuid = <fs_dir>-eltuid.
    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND ( <fs_calc>-aggrexc IS NOT INITIAL OR <fs_calc>-aggrgen IS NOT INITIAL ).
      lv_has_calc = abap_true.
    ENDIF.

    IF lv_formula IS INITIAL AND lv_has_filters = abap_false AND lv_has_calc = abap_false.
      CONTINUE.
    ENDIF.

    lv_count = lv_count + 1.

    PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_desc.
    PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_disp_name.

    IF lv_formula IS NOT INITIAL.
      IF lv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
        lv_line = |\\b { lv_count }) { lv_disp_name }\\b0  ({ lv_desc }) = { lv_formula }\\par|.
      ELSE.
        lv_line = |\\b { lv_count }) { lv_disp_name }\\b0 = { lv_formula }\\par|.
      ENDIF.
    ELSE.
      IF lv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
        lv_line = |\\b { lv_count }) { lv_disp_name }\\b0  ({ lv_desc })\\par|.
      ELSE.
        lv_line = |\\b { lv_count }) { lv_disp_name }\\b0\\par|.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    APPEND lv_line TO ct_doc.

    IF lv_has_calc = abap_true.
      CLEAR lv_aggr_type.
      IF <fs_calc>-aggrexc IS NOT INITIAL.
        CASE <fs_calc>-aggrexc.
          WHEN 'CN0' OR '000'. lv_aggr_type = 'Counter (All Values)'.
          WHEN 'CNT' OR '001'. lv_aggr_type = 'Counter (Values Unequal to Zero)'.
          WHEN 'SUM' OR '002'. lv_aggr_type = 'Summation'.
          WHEN 'AVG' OR '003'. lv_aggr_type = 'Average'.
          WHEN 'MIN' OR '004'. lv_aggr_type = 'Minimum'.
          WHEN 'MAX' OR '005'. lv_aggr_type = 'Maximum'.
          WHEN 'NOP' OR '006'. lv_aggr_type = 'No Aggregation'.
          WHEN OTHERS.        lv_aggr_type = <fs_calc>-aggrexc.
        ENDCASE.

        IF <fs_calc>-aggrcha IS NOT INITIAL.
          APPEND |  \\i Exception Aggregation: { lv_aggr_type } ({ <fs_calc>-aggrcha })\\i0\\par| TO ct_doc.
        ELSE.
          APPEND |  \\i Exception Aggregation: { lv_aggr_type }\\i0\\par| TO ct_doc.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    LOOP AT g_th_range ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_rng>)
         WHERE eltuid = <fs_dir>-eltuid.

      DATA(lv_res_val) = <fs_rng>-low.
      PERFORM resolve_filter_value
        USING    <fs_rng>-low
        CHANGING lv_res_val.
      PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_res_val.

      DATA(lv_sign) = COND string(
        WHEN <fs_rng>-sign = 'E' THEN 'Exclude (E)'
        ELSE 'Include (I)' ).

      DATA(lv_opt) = COND string(
        WHEN <fs_rng>-opt IS NOT INITIAL THEN <fs_rng>-opt
        ELSE 'EQ' ).

      IF <fs_rng>-high IS NOT INITIAL.
        DATA(lv_high_val) = <fs_rng>-high.
        PERFORM resolve_filter_value USING <fs_rng>-high CHANGING lv_high_val.
        PERFORM escape_rtf CHANGING lv_high_val.
        lv_res_val = |{ lv_res_val } - { lv_high_val }|.
      ENDIF.

      APPEND |  \\i Filter -> Field: { <fs_rng>-iobjnm } \| Sign: { lv_sign } \| Opt: { lv_opt } \| Value: { lv_res_val }\\i0\\par| TO ct_doc.
    ENDLOOP.

    APPEND '\line' TO ct_doc.

  ENDLOOP.

  IF lv_count = 0.
    APPEND '  No explicit RKF, CKF, Local Selection, or Formula definitions found in query metadata.\par' TO ct_doc.
  ENDIF.

  APPEND '}\par' TO ct_doc.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RECONSTRUCT_FORMULA_TREE
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM reconstruct_formula_tree USING    VALUE(i_uid)   TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                             CHANGING cv_formula    TYPE string.

  DATA: lt_stages TYPE tt_rszcalc,
        ls_stage  TYPE rszcalc.

  CLEAR cv_formula.

  LOOP AT g_th_calc INTO ls_stage WHERE eltuid = i_uid.
    APPEND ls_stage TO lt_stages.
  ENDLOOP.

  IF lt_stages IS INITIAL.
    SELECT *
      FROM rszcalc
      INTO TABLE @LT_stages
      WHERE eltuid  = @i_uid
        AND objvers = 'A'.
  ENDIF.

  IF lt_stages IS INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  SORT lt_stages BY stepnr ASCENDING.

  PERFORM resolve_calc_stage
    USING    i_uid
             '001'
             lt_stages
    CHANGING cv_formula.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RESOLVE_CALC_STAGE
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM resolve_calc_stage USING    VALUE(i_uid)     TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid
                                 VALUE(i_step)    TYPE any
                                 it_stages        TYPE tt_rszcalc
                        CHANGING cv_expr          TYPE string.

  DATA: ls_calc  TYPE rszcalc,
        lv_left  TYPE string,
        lv_right TYPE string,
        lv_step  TYPE rszcalc-stepnr.

  CLEAR cv_expr.

  lv_step = |{ i_step ALPHA = IN }|.

  READ TABLE it_stages INTO ls_calc WITH KEY stepnr = lv_step.
  IF sy-subrc <> 0.
    READ TABLE it_stages INTO ls_calc WITH KEY stepnr = i_step.
    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  IF ls_calc-o1flg = 'H'.
    PERFORM resolve_calc_stage USING i_uid ls_calc-oper1 it_stages CHANGING lv_left.
  ELSEIF ls_calc-oper1 IS NOT INITIAL.
    PERFORM format_operand USING ls_calc-o1flg ls_calc-oper1 CHANGING lv_left.
  ENDIF.

  IF ls_calc-o2flg = 'H'.
    PERFORM resolve_calc_stage USING i_uid ls_calc-oper2 it_stages CHANGING lv_right.
  ELSEIF ls_calc-oper2 IS NOT INITIAL.
    PERFORM format_operand USING ls_calc-o2flg ls_calc-oper2 CHANGING lv_right.
  ENDIF.

  DATA(lv_op) = ls_calc-opera.
  CONDENSE lv_op.

  CASE lv_op.
    WHEN '/' OR '004' OR 'DIV'.
      cv_expr = |{ lv_left } / { lv_right }|.
    WHEN '*' OR '003' OR 'MUL'.
      cv_expr = |{ lv_left } * { lv_right }|.
    WHEN '+' OR '002' OR 'ADD'.
      cv_expr = |{ lv_left } + { lv_right }|.
    WHEN '-' OR '001' OR 'SUB'.
      cv_expr = |{ lv_left } - { lv_right }|.
    WHEN 'NDIV0'.
      cv_expr = |NDIV0({ lv_left })|.
    WHEN 'NODIM'.
      cv_expr = |NODIM({ lv_left })|.
    WHEN 'ABS'.
      cv_expr = |ABS({ lv_left })|.
    WHEN 'SQRT'.
      cv_expr = |SQRT({ lv_left })|.
    WHEN 'TIME'.
      cv_expr = |TIME({ lv_left })|.
    WHEN 'DATE'.
      cv_expr = |DATE({ lv_left })|.
    WHEN OTHERS.
      IF lv_op IS NOT INITIAL.
        IF lv_right IS NOT INITIAL.
          cv_expr = |{ lv_op }({ lv_left }, { lv_right })|.
        ELSEIF lv_left IS NOT INITIAL.
          cv_expr = |{ lv_op }({ lv_left })|.
        ELSE.
          cv_expr = lv_op.
        ENDIF.
      ELSE.
        cv_expr = lv_left.
      ENDIF.
  ENDCASE.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RESOLVE_DEFAULTHINT
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM resolve_defaulthint USING    iv_hint TYPE any
                         CHANGING cv_desc TYPE string.

  DATA: lv_hint_str TYPE string,
        lv_iobj     TYPE rsdiobjnm.

  CLEAR cv_desc.
  lv_hint_str = iv_hint.
  IF lv_hint_str IS INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_txt>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = lv_hint_str.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_txt>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_desc = <fs_txt>-txtlg.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  SELECT SINGLE txtlg
    FROM rszelttxt
    INTO @CV_desc
    WHERE eltuid  = @LV_hint_str
      AND langu   = @SY-langu
      AND objvers = 'A'.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND cv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  lv_iobj = lv_hint_str.
  IF lv_hint_str CA '-'.
    SPLIT lv_hint_str AT '-' INTO DATA(lv_prefix) DATA(lv_suffix).
    IF lv_suffix IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_iobj = lv_suffix.
    ENDIF.
  ELSEIF strlen( lv_hint_str ) > 1 AND lv_hint_str(1) = '4'.
    lv_iobj = lv_hint_str+1.
  ENDIF.

  SELECT SINGLE txtlg
    FROM rsdiobjt
    INTO @CV_desc
    WHERE iobjnm  = @LV_iobj
      AND langu   = @SY-langu
      AND objvers = 'A'.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND cv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  SELECT SINGLE txtsh
    FROM rsdiobjt
    INTO @CV_desc
    WHERE iobjnm  = @LV_iobj
      AND langu   = @SY-langu
      AND objvers = 'A'.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND cv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  cv_desc = lv_hint_str.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: FORMAT_OPERAND
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM format_operand USING    VALUE(iv_flg)  TYPE rszcalc-o1flg
                             VALUE(iv_oper) TYPE rszcalc-oper1
                    CHANGING cv_text        TYPE string.

  DATA: lv_uid      TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid,
        lv_tech     TYPE string,
        lv_desc     TYPE string,
        lv_raw_oper TYPE string.

  CLEAR cv_text.
  lv_raw_oper = iv_oper.
  CONDENSE lv_raw_oper.

  IF iv_flg = 'C' OR ( lv_raw_oper CO '0123456789. ' AND strlen( lv_raw_oper ) < 15 ).
    cv_text = lv_raw_oper.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  lv_uid = lv_raw_oper.

  READ TABLE g_th_compdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_cdir>) WITH KEY compuid = lv_uid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_cdir>-compid IS NOT INITIAL.
    lv_tech = <fs_cdir>-compid.
  ELSE.
    SELECT SINGLE compid
      FROM rszcompdir
      INTO @LV_tech
      WHERE compuid = @LV_uid
        AND objvers = 'A'.
  ENDIF.

  IF lv_tech IS INITIAL.
    READ TABLE g_th_globv ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_globv>)
         WITH KEY varuniid = lv_uid.
    IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_globv>-vnam IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_tech = <fs_globv>-vnam.
    ELSE.
      SELECT SINGLE vnam
        FROM rszglobv
        INTO @LV_tech
        WHERE varuniid = @LV_uid
          AND objvers  = 'A'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDIF.

  IF lv_tech IS INITIAL.
    lv_tech = lv_uid.
  ENDIF.

  READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_txt>)
       WITH KEY eltuid = lv_uid.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_txt>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
    lv_desc = <fs_txt>-txtlg.
  ELSE.
    SELECT SINGLE txtlg
      FROM rszelttxt
      INTO @LV_desc
      WHERE eltuid  = @LV_uid
        AND langu   = @SY-langu
        AND objvers = 'A'.
  ENDIF.

  READ TABLE g_th_eltdir ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_dir>) WITH KEY eltuid = lv_uid.
  IF lv_desc IS INITIAL AND <fs_dir> IS ASSIGNED AND <fs_dir>-defaulthint IS NOT INITIAL.
    PERFORM resolve_defaulthint USING <fs_dir>-defaulthint CHANGING lv_desc.
  ENDIF.

  IF lv_desc IS INITIAL AND lv_tech IS NOT INITIAL AND lv_tech <> lv_uid.
    SELECT SINGLE txtlg
      FROM rsdiobjt
      INTO @LV_desc
      WHERE iobjnm  = @LV_tech
        AND langu   = @SY-langu
        AND objvers = 'A'.
  ENDIF.

  IF lv_tech IS NOT INITIAL AND lv_desc IS NOT INITIAL AND lv_tech <> lv_desc.
    cv_text = |"[{ lv_tech }] { lv_desc }"|.
  ELSEIF lv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_text = |"[{ lv_uid }] { lv_desc }"|.
  ELSEIF lv_tech IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_text = |"[{ lv_tech }]"|.
  ELSE.
    cv_text = |"{ lv_uid }"|.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RESOLVE_FILTER_VALUE
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM resolve_filter_value USING    VALUE(iv_raw_val) TYPE any
                          CHANGING cv_resolved_val   TYPE string.

  DATA: lv_val TYPE string,
        lv_uid TYPE rszeltdir-eltuid.

  lv_val = iv_raw_val.
  cv_resolved_val = lv_val.

  IF lv_val IS INITIAL.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  READ TABLE g_th_globv ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_globv>)
       WITH KEY varuniid = lv_val.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_globv>-vnam IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_resolved_val = <fs_globv>-vnam.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  lv_uid = lv_val.
  SELECT SINGLE compid
    FROM rszcompdir
    INTO @DATA(lv_db_compid)
    WHERE compuid = @LV_uid
      AND objvers = 'A'.
  IF sy-subrc = 0 AND lv_db_compid IS NOT INITIAL.
    cv_resolved_val = lv_db_compid.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: ESCAPE_RTF
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM escape_rtf CHANGING cv_text TYPE any.

  DATA lv_text TYPE string.

  lv_text = cv_text.

  REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF '\' IN lv_text WITH '\\'.
  REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF '{' IN lv_text WITH '\{'.
  REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF '}' IN lv_text WITH '\}'.

  cv_text = lv_text.

ENDFORM.

*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
*& Subroutine: RESOLVE_TEXT_VARIABLES
*&---------------------------------------------------------------------*
FORM resolve_text_variables CHANGING cv_text TYPE string.

  DATA: lt_results TYPE match_result_tab,
        ls_match   TYPE match_result,
        lv_varname TYPE rszcompdir-compid,
        lv_var_spc TYPE rszcompdir-compid,
        lv_replace TYPE string,
        lv_desc    TYPE string,
        lv_target  TYPE string.

  IF cv_text IS INITIAL OR cv_text NA '&'.
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  FIND ALL OCCURRENCES OF REGEX '&([A-Za-z0-9_]+)&' IN cv_text RESULTS lt_results.

  LOOP AT lt_results INTO ls_match.
    DATA(ls_submatch) = ls_match-submatches[ 1 ].
    lv_varname = cv_text+ls_submatch-offset(ls_submatch-length).

    CLEAR: lv_desc, lv_replace.

    READ TABLE g_th_globv ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_globv>)
         WITH KEY vnam = lv_varname.

    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      READ TABLE g_th_elttxt ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_gtxt>)
           WITH KEY eltuid = <fs_globv>-varuniid.
      IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_gtxt>-txtlg IS NOT INITIAL.
        lv_desc = <fs_gtxt>-txtlg.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    IF lv_desc IS INITIAL.
      lv_var_spc = REPLACE( val = CONV string( lv_varname ) sub = '_' with = ' ' occ = 0 ).

      SELECT SINGLE t~txtlg
        FROM rszcompdir AS c
        INNER JOIN rszelttxt AS t
           ON c~compuid = t~eltuid
          AND c~objvers = t~objvers
        INTO @LV_desc
        WHERE ( c~compid = @LV_varname OR c~compid = @LV_var_spc )
          AND c~objvers  = 'A'
          AND t~langu    = @SY-langu.
    ENDIF.

    IF lv_desc IS INITIAL.
      SELECT SINGLE t~txtlg
        FROM rszcompdir AS c
        INNER JOIN rszelttxt AS t
           ON c~compuid = t~eltuid
          AND c~objvers = t~objvers
        INTO @LV_desc
        WHERE ( c~compid = @LV_varname OR c~compid = @LV_var_spc )
          AND c~objvers  = 'A'.
    ENDIF.

    IF lv_desc IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_replace = |{ lv_varname } ({ lv_desc })|.
    ELSE.
      lv_replace = lv_varname.
    ENDIF.

    lv_target = |&{ lv_varname }&|.
    REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF lv_target IN cv_text WITH lv_replace.
  ENDLOOP.

ENDFORM.
